newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan in secret summit over row - paper.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan in secret summit over row - paper.

text.p: Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein met secretly in Jordan on Thursday night to try to patch up a row over water, the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth said on Friday.
The daily, Israel's biggest, said Netanyahu flew by military helicopter with close advisers and high-ranking army officers to the summit at the Red Sea port of Aqaba.
The paper quoted Netanyahu's spokesman as neither confirming nor denying a meeting took place.
According to the report, Netanyahu and the king discussed reviving Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations and the water dispute.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan cancelled a meeting on Tuesday with Netanyahu because of disagreements over water supplies promised to the Arab kingdom under their 1994 peace treaty.

Jordanian officials accused Israel of backing out at the last minute from an accord to fulfil its pledge under the treaty to help the kingdom, facing growing water shortages, find an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year.
The treaty, ending a 46-year state of war, specified that within a year of its coming into force in November 1994 the two sides would develop a plan to supply Jordan with the water.
Ideas for the water supply included desalination plants, dam building, and steps to ease pollution of river waters. But no plan was formally implemented.

Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh spoke this week of a "frustration in the whole peace process" among Jordanians, and said Israel's failure to follow up its commitment to help find water supplies for Jordan was a breach of the 1994 treaty.

In Jerusalem and the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip on Thursday, U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross appeared to be making little progress in his latest mission to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations.
"I cannot tell you that I am optimistic," Netanyahu told reporters in Israel on Thursday evening.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down two months ago after Netanyahu gave the final go-ahead for the construction of 6,500 houses for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem on land claimed by both sides.
Ross, on his second mission in a month, met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Gaza and Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Thursday.
